title: 2:1 Multiplexer (Data Selector)
summary: A Multiplexer (MUX) is a combinational circuit that selects one of several data input lines and routes it to a single output line based on Select line signals.

images.title: 2:1 MUX Symbol
images.caption: Data inputs I0, I1, Select line S, and Output Y.

images.title: Gate Schematic
images.caption: 2:1 MUX using 1 NOT (7404), 2 AND (7408), and 1 OR (7432).

images.title: ANSI Logic Symbol
images.caption: ANSI standard block symbol for Multiplexer.

working_principle: Equation: Y = S'·I0 + S·I1. When S=0, input I0 is routed to Y. When S=1, input I1 is routed to Y.
applications: Data Bus Steering and Routing in CPUs
advantages: Acts as a universal logic generator for N-variable functions
disadvantages: Adds propagation delay to data signal paths
common_mistakes: Confusing Select line S with Data input lines I0 and I1.
quick_notes: 2:1 MUX has 2 data inputs, 1 select line, 1 output.
N select lines can route 2^N data inputs.

viva_questions.q: What is the relation between number of data inputs and select lines in a MUX?
viva_questions.a: If there are N select lines, the MUX can select from 2^N data inputs.

viva_questions.q: How can a MUX be used as a universal logic generator?
viva_questions.a: By connecting Boolean variables to select lines and tieing data inputs to 0, 1, or remaining variables.

interview_questions.q: How many 2:1 MUXes are required to build a 4:1 MUX?
interview_questions.a: 3 2:1 MUXes (2 in first stage, 1 in second stage).
